speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. To understand the nature of your chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis, I need to ask a few targeted questions. How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and do you notice any specific triggers like exercise, cold air, or lying down?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. Your history of a chronic productive cough for over a decade with recurrent "bronchitis" despite antibiotic treatment is highly characteristic of this condition. I need to confirm if you have ever been diagnosed with tuberculosis or suffered significant pneumonia, and do you notice any shortness of breath or hemoptysis (coughing up blood)?
